evidence.claim: Brazil began discussions with the IAEA on safeguards arrangements for fuel in its nuclear submarine project, and Reuters notes that such submarines pose a special proliferation-monitoring challenge.
evidence.title: Brasil inicia negociação com AIEA sobre combustível para projeto de submarino nuclear
evidence.excerpt: Brazil began discussions with the IAEA on safeguards arrangements for fuel in its nuclear submarine project, and Reuters notes that such submarines pose a special proliferation-monitoring challenge.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting via a major local-language outlet; strong but secondary and not official.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Administration-level policy choice under Bolsonaro; the article does not show personal direction.
contrary_evidence: The article concerns a propulsion/fuel safeguards issue, not nuclear weapons acquisition.

evidence.claim: Brazil and Argentina voluntarily requested IAEA safeguards within the ABACC system and the treaty text emphasizes peaceful use and avoiding unnecessary duplication of safeguards work.
evidence.title: Agreement between Brazil, Argentina, the ABACC and the IAEA (Quadripartite Agreement)
evidence.publication_date: treaty text current on ABACC site
evidence.excerpt: Brazil and Argentina voluntarily requested IAEA safeguards within the ABACC system and the treaty text emphasizes peaceful use and avoiding unnecessary duplication of safeguards work.
evidence.source_locator: Preamble text on the agreement page
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official regional safeguards body reproducing the agreement text.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Institutional baseline, not personal Bolsonaro conduct.
contrary_evidence: Safeguards architecture constrains risk but does not eliminate all dual-use concerns.

evidence.claim: Brazil's representative associated Brazil with the New Agenda Coalition and called the Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons one of the great recent achievements in disarmament.
evidence.title: Nuclear-Weapon States Have Special Responsibility to Advance Non-Proliferation, Disarmament, Speakers Stress on Day Three of Review Conference
evidence.excerpt: Brazil's representative associated Brazil with the New Agenda Coalition and called the Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons one of the great recent achievements in disarmament.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous UN meeting record with attributed national statement.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Brazilian government diplomacy under Bolsonaro; the statement is institutional, not a personal Bolsonaro quote.
contrary_evidence: Diplomatic support does not prove deeper internal commitment or implementation at cabinet level.

evidence.claim: Brazil's representative said the use of nuclear arms is comparable to a crime against humanity and condemned explicit or implicit nuclear threats.
evidence.title: Non-Nuclear-Armed States Get Nothing in Return for Fulfilling Commitments Except Threat of Potential Annihilation, First Committee Told
evidence.excerpt: Brazil's representative said the use of nuclear arms is comparable to a crime against humanity and condemned explicit or implicit nuclear threats.
evidence.source_locator: Statement by Ronaldo Roberto Bonzanini / Brazil in the meeting coverage
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous UN meeting coverage with attributed national statement.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Brazilian government statement under Bolsonaro's administration; not a private Bolsonaro statement.
contrary_evidence: The statement is normative diplomacy, not proof of operational de-escalation in a crisis.

evidence.claim: Brazil condemned North Korea's ICBM launch as destabilizing and urged states to redouble efforts toward the CTBT and NPT.
evidence.title: The Brazilian Government has condemned the launch of an intercontinental ballistic missile by the Democratic People's Republic of Korea
evidence.excerpt: Brazil condemned North Korea's ICBM launch as destabilizing and urged states to redouble efforts toward the CTBT and NPT.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official Brazilian government note released in 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Government-level attribution under Bolsonaro; not a personal quote from Bolsonaro.
contrary_evidence: The statement addresses another state's launch, not Bolsonaro's own crisis behavior.

evidence.claim: Brazil produced its first national report on threats to nuclear physical security, describing state-intelligence work on sabotage and illicit acquisition risks to guide a design-basis threat process.
evidence.title: Brasil passa a contar com relatório de ameaças à segurança física nuclear
evidence.excerpt: Brazil produced its first national report on threats to nuclear physical security, describing state-intelligence work on sabotage and illicit acquisition risks to guide a design-basis threat process.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official intelligence-agency announcement with clear operational description.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Government institution under Bolsonaro; indicates risk-management capacity rather than personal rhetoric.
contrary_evidence: A threat report indicates vulnerability assessment, not necessarily successful risk reduction by itself.

evidence.claim: Brazil said the Conference on Disarmament should not be abandoned and supported continued work on a fissile-material treaty and broader disarmament diplomacy.
evidence.title: Brazil's representative at the First Committee on 4 November 2022
evidence.excerpt: Brazil said the Conference on Disarmament should not be abandoned and supported continued work on a fissile-material treaty and broader disarmament diplomacy.
evidence.source_locator: Brazil statement in the meeting coverage
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous UN meeting coverage with attributed Brazilian statement.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Brazilian diplomatic posture under Bolsonaro's administration; not a personal Bolsonaro quote.
contrary_evidence: This is process-oriented diplomacy rather than evidence of concrete risk reduction at home.
